subject.title: [Feature]: Include interaction metadata in Discord button callbacks

question: Should generic Discord component callbacks expose a new agent-visible structured interaction metadata envelope, and which fields are public versus plugin-only?
rationale: This changes the public agent inbound context and exposes Discord identifiers/callback data, so maintainers need to choose schema shape, compatibility behavior, privacy/security boundary, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Add Typed Agent Metadata
options.body: Expose a narrow documented envelope with message id, action kind, safe callback/custom data, label/value details, and clicker identity, backed by Discord plugin tests.

options.title: Keep Metadata Plugin-Only
options.body: Leave rich interaction fields only in plugin interactive handlers and document that stateful Discord workflows should use plugin callbacks instead of generic fallback messages.

options.title: Start With Sender And Message
options.body: Expose only clicker and originating message ids first, deferring callback payload semantics until a broader inbound metadata contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Add Typed Agent Metadata
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow documented envelope with message id, action kind, safe callback/custom data, label/value details, and clicker identity, backed by Discord plugin tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The Discord component callback surface traces back to their Components v2 work, making them the strongest history-backed routing candidate for the API direction.
